recipes.title: Plotter edition
recipes.plain: A drawing a pen machine can make
recipes.how: Seeded p5.js sketch, exported as SVG paths, cleaned with vpype, drawn on an AxiDraw. Plot time per token is the real cost [estimate].
recipes.publish: Code project on Art Blocks (Studio) or ABX (deploy-code). To mark a token as plotted: PostParams on Art Blocks Flex, or a typed parameter on ABX [sourced features; the plotted flag is our suggestion].

recipes.title: 3D-printed object
recipes.how: three.js scene from the token seed, exported as an .obj or STL, printed in FDM or resin. Collectors rarely own printers, so finishing is the product [estimate].
recipes.publish: Keep the export in the script so the token is the fabrication file (7 verified Art Blocks tokens do this) [AB data].

recipes.title: Chip-verified physical with redemption state
recipes.plain: A physical piece you can tap to check
recipes.how: Plot or print each output, attach an NFC tag, and on redemption record 'issued' plus the chip ID as per-token state.
recipes.publish: Today: Art Blocks PostParams or an ABX typed parameter can hold that state [sourced features]. Next: ERC-8048 keys such as physical and chip [our inference: neither Art Blocks nor ABX documents ERC-8048].

recipes.title: Slow token on an e-ink frame
recipes.plain: A picture that changes slowly on a paper-like screen
recipes.how: Clock-driven sketch that changes hourly, shown on a colour e-ink panel with an ESP32 (about $100 [estimate], SRB).
recipes.publish: A standard code project on either platform; the frame only needs the live view URL.

recipes.title: Generative sound piece
recipes.how: Web Audio graph seeded by the token hash; start sound on a tap because browsers block autoplay [estimate].
recipes.publish: Code project; on Art Blocks, libraries can come from the on-chain Dependency Registry [sourced].

recipes.title: Embroidered patch edition
recipes.plain: A stitched patch from a file
recipes.how: SVG paths into Ink/Stitch (an Inkscape extension) to make a stitch file for an embroidery machine. {LOGO} made embroidery export a token feature [sourced].
recipes.publish: Code project that offers the stitch file as an output; physical redemption tracked with PostParams or an ABX parameter [our suggestion].

recipes.title: Token as agent (experimental)
recipes.plain: A token that can act on its own
recipes.how: On a testnet: a generative ERC-721 that also carries 721T keys (context, endpoint[web]) read through ERC-8048 metadata(), plus an ERC-6551 account so the piece can hold things.
recipes.publish: ERC-6551 works with existing ERC-721s without contract changes per its spec [sourced], so an Art Blocks or ABX token could get an account [our inference]. 721T needs a contract that implements ERC-8048; neither platform documents that [our check].
recipes.status: Whitespace (Shawn's idea); no Art Blocks use found

paths.blurb: Start with a picture. Send it to a pen plotter or a print studio.
Embroidery, weaving, and knitting. The file is often stitches or a thread grid.
Print, cut, cast, or build a physical thing from the file.
Sound made in the browser, from the same seed as the picture.
Code that draws in a browser, a projector, a headset, or a frame at home.
Pieces that shift with the clock, the season, or what happens after mint.

paths.plain: Things that act on their own
paths.blurb: A token that can hold things or speak for the work. Experimental.

intro: **What it does.** ABX is "an open-source protocol and toolkit for putting digital objects on the blockchain". [sourced: https://www.abx.io/ (agent view https://abx.io/?view=agent), https://docs.abx.io/llms.txt]
**Who runs it.** It is "Maintained by the team at Art Blocks" / "Built by the team at Art Blocks". [sourced: abx.io]

**License.** The repo is https://github.com/ArtBlocks/abx, MIT license, created 2026-09-09 UTC. Its repo description reads "Open protocol and toolkit for creating, operating, and serving NFTs". [sourced: GitHub API]

**Announcement.** Art Blocks announced ABX on X on Sep 30, 2026: https://x.com/artblocks_io/status/2105359383626445289. The announcement also says the curated flagship artblocks.io continues with its existing standards. [sourced: X post, read earlier in this task]

**Status.** abx.io calls it "prerelease software, not independently audited". The docs say: "ABX has not had an independent third-party audit." and "Beta networks use real funds and irreversible state while ABX remains pre-1.0." [sourced: abx.io; https://docs.abx.io/docs/reference/deployments]

abx.pluginLead: None of ERC-8048, 721T, ERC-6551, ERC-8004, ERC-8217 or ERC-7160 appears in the ABX docs or in the Art Blocks docs we read. Every mapping below is our inference unless it is tagged [sourced].

plugins.title: ERC-8048 (redemption or evolving state)
plugins.body: Today, the same per-token state fits in Art Blocks PostParams [sourced feature] or ABX typed parameters and field renderers [sourced feature]. Native ERC-8048 would need a contract that implements `metadata(tokenId,key)` and `MetadataSet` [spec]; neither platform documents that.

plugins.title: 721T
plugins.body: It needs an ERC-8048 contract [spec: https://github.com/nxt3d/721t]. It is not documented on either platform.

plugins.title: ERC-6551
plugins.body: The spec says it works with existing ERC-721s without contract changes [sourced: https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-6551]. ABX series and code projects are ERC-721 [sourced], and so are Art Blocks tokens. So both could get token-bound accounts [our inference].

plugins.title: ERC-8217
plugins.body: It binds existing NFTs to ERC-8004 agents without changing the collection [spec], so the platform does not matter [our inference].

plugins.title: IPFS / Arweave and fully on-chain
plugins.body: Both are [sourced] on both platforms; see the table.

uncertainties: **Status.** ABX is prerelease and pre-1.0, with no third-party audit, and its production networks are in beta.
**Fees.** No ABX fee schedule was found, and hosted-service sponsorship "may be limited".
**Sales.** ABX ships only fixed-price sales. Auctions and allowlists need custom contracts.
**Art Blocks gap.** The Art Blocks pages we read do not describe script freezing or locking.
**Launch details.** The Sep 30 date and the line about the flagship continuing come from the @artblocks_io X post. We did not use an artblocks.io blog post as a source.
